claims.text: install-git-hooks.sh is a no-op on rerun when both stubs carry their marker and the same plugin-root line; a second run printed 'already installed' and left both files byte-identical.

install-git-hooks.sh never checks the stub write: when the write fails it still prints 'installed' and exits 0 (also without --quiet), the stale stub keeps the old plugin root, and the H5 probe still passes.

A pre-existing non-AFK hook is kept: exit 1 without --quiet, exit 0 with a stderr notice under --quiet, and the other hook is still installed; the H5 probe reads only reference-transaction, so a kept foreign pre-commit leaves H5 ok while the commit gates are absent.

With core.hooksPath set the installer writes nothing and exits 0 with a stderr notice; the H5 probe then reads the hooksPath folder and fails, so H5 cannot flip to ok and the walk reports it needs-human (classification inferred from SKILL.md step 5).

The git hooks live in the git common dir's hooks folder, outside the working tree, and cover every worktree; the installer writes no git config; no plugin command removes them; the only stated undo is removing the files by hand; a stub whose gate file is gone exits 0.

Every Claude and Codex session start re-runs install-git-hooks.sh --quiet under run-hook.py --soft, so it never fails the session and re-installs a hook removed by hand while the plugin stays enabled; whether the harness shows its stderr notice is unverified.

afk-config.py init refuses an existing file (exit 2, nothing written) and a config on the base branch or main worktree; it writes only <root>/.afk/config.yaml; it writes before it validates, so an invalid scaffold stays on disk with exit 2; a write error is an uncaught traceback, exit 1.

developer_values.py set rewrites <git common dir>/afk/config.yaml (or ~/.afk/config.yaml with --machine) byte-identically on rerun through temp + replace; it drops comments inside the developer: block and moves the block to the end; an OSError is uncaught (exit 1) and leaves config.yaml.tmp; undo is KEY= per key.

install_block.py install is idempotent (already-current, same bytes); teardown is the H7 undo but not a byte-exact inverse: the separator and trailing newline install appended stay, a file install created stays as one newline, and a .<name>.afk.lock file stays beside each target, created even by teardown of an absent target.
install_block.py into a read-only target exits 2 with the target unchanged but leaves a .<name>.<random>.tmp file beside it.
The H7 recipe exits 1 at the first target that fails, after earlier targets were written; a rerun refreshes them in place.

setup_secrets.py refuses an agent shell only when CLAUDECODE is set; it has no tty check and ran to exit 0 with its one confirmation answered on a pipe, so SKILL.md's 'no tty' refusal is not in the code.

setup_secrets.py writes ~/.claude.json from Path.home() and ignores CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; each run that reaches the tracker leg adds a new .claude.json.bak-<timestamp> copy that nothing prunes, while .claude.json itself stays byte-identical on rerun.

Each backup is a whole-file copy of ~/.claude.json, so under tracker jira it also holds JIRA_API_TOKEN in plain text (inferred from shutil.copy2 of the file the token is written into; not run with a token).

setup_secrets.py runs tracker, then forge login, then long paths, then re-probe; a die() or an uncaught error (EOF at a prompt, a ConfigError in any config layer, a failed git config) exits 1 and skips every later leg, and a tracker entry written earlier stays written.

Outside the repository setup_secrets.py writes ~/.claude.json mcpServers.tracker, its backups, the forge CLI's own credential store through 'gh|glab auth login', and git config --global core.longpaths true; no plugin command undoes any of them.

H1, H4, S2 and S3 write nothing during setup.
tracker_registration.register is pure and idempotent: two calls give the same entry, a foreign jira entry is kept as it was, and afk's own legacy jira entry is dropped with its env carried over.
